text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures digested a mound of economic news but at the end of the day found little reason to stray far from where they opened. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.56, down 0.06 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled slightly lower as a lack of domestic fundamental news left them following shaky technicals and slipping overseas markets. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-9/32, down 1/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures settled higher after a weak start but remained vulnerable, like their U.S. and German counterparts, ahead of Friday U.S. payroll data preceded by U.S. producer price and German jobless data on Thursday. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.02, up 0.16 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures closed firmer but off session highs in a quiet, cautious market stuck in a narrow range awaiting domestic economic and political developments. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.71, up 0.42 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened generally unchanged Tuesday, as market participants said they are content to wait for key economic releases later in the week before taking on any new positions. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-28/32, down 13/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.8 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended up, but off the day's highs as a plunge in Tokyo share prices towards the close pared gains. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 124.33, up 0.57 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Dollar and sterling Eurobonds dominated a hectic day in the Eurobond market, with over 30 new issues. Exim Bank of Japan launched a 400 million stg 10-year institutional deal, and other borrowers issued shorter-dated retail-targeted sterling bonds. The largest dollar deal was a $500 million three-year issue for Abbey National. The European Investment Bank will launch a 500 million stg bond due June 2002 soon. On Wednesday Mexico will issue a $1.0 bln 10-year global.
